body:
Fixes #2267.

## What happened

A successful `/codex` completion contained an older Claude access report in its transcript. The Telegram parser searched for the legacy marker anywhere in a line, so quoted JSON, diffs, and historical logs could be mistaken for the current run. It then consumed unrelated trailing output into an oversized false alert.

When that oversized edit was split, the follow-up `sendMessage` did not retain the forum topic ID and landed in the chat's general topic.

The existing wording also described inactive access to one tool as a blocked account, which was stronger than the provider response supported.

I audited both attached incident logs. Each contains a real Claude HTTP 403 with `oauth_org_not_allowed`, but no Codex subscription failure. The other warnings/errors are expected attach-log notices, exploratory commands, approval checks, or test iterations that continued; they are not missed subscription failures.

## What changed

- Replay an access report only for a failed completion and only when its tool matches the current session.
- Recognize markers only at the beginning of a captured log payload, while still parsing timestamp/level-prefixed reports and the legacy marker.
- Say that tool subscription/access is unavailable and that the provider supplied no reset time; do not claim the whole account is blocked.
- Apply the neutral wording in English, Russian, Chinese, and Hindi.
- Persist `message_thread_id` for direct, queued, and isolated sessions and retain it for overflow follow-ups (while omitting it from `editMessageText`, where Telegram does not accept it).
- Update the existing npm-link regression for npm 12's new, explicit "install scripts blocked" behavior exposed by the current Node 24.21 base; the repository's `--ignore-scripts` requirement is unchanged.

## Reproduction and result

Before, a successful Codex completion could replay a quoted Claude failure:

![Successful Codex completion with a stale Claude access alert](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f09ff9d4-2211-40b9-940c-83b0ae20023f)

The overflow could then appear in the general topic:

![Unexpected output in the Telegram general topic](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a06e97cd-87ae-4a3f-a66e-6809350cdfe1)

After, successful sessions do not produce an access alert. A current failed Claude session is reported without the account-level claim:

```text
⚠️ Tool subscription/access unavailable
CLAUDE: Subscription access is inactive for this organization
Why the run stopped: The provider reports that this organization's subscription access to the selected tool is inactive. This does not mean the whole account is blocked, and the provider did not give a reset time.
```

Any split follow-up remains in the originating Telegram topic.

## Tests

- `node tests/inactive-subscription-2267.test.mjs` — 11/11 regression cases
- `node tests/subscription-error-2161.test.mjs` — 42/42 existing subscription cases
- both attached incident logs replayed: Claude failure detected; Codex and successful-session sections empty
- `bash scripts/test-telegram-bot-execution.sh`
- npm-link regression — 12/12 on npm 12.0.2
- `npm test` — 493/493 test files after merging current `main`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- syntax, file-line-limit, package-manager, changeset, duplication, and secret checks
title: fix: avoid stale inactive-subscription alerts
